title: Mixed SKU allocation scenario matrix — Private VPC BOM & headroom model
summary: A working spreadsheet that models mixed-GPU SKU allocations across regions for Private/VPC deployments. Produces a scenario matrix (performance, cost, utilization, headroom) and recommended BOM per scenario with sensitivity to quantization, batch sizing, and KV-cache hit rates.
intended_audience: Private deploy eng, infra procurement, solutions engineering, customer success
scenarios: Baseline steady-state: 60% target utilization, even latency distribution, 12k qps-equivalent tokens/day
90th-percentile surge: short spikes 3x baseline for up to 4 hours/day (regional), test headroom sizing
Latency-sensitive edge: strict 99th pctl < 120ms, prefer low-latency SKUs and regional replication
Cost-optimized quantized: heavy INT8/4 usage, tolerate slightly higher 99th pctl for 35% lower per-token cost
Heterogeneous fallback: mix of high-memory H100s for long-context models + cheaper A10/A100 for short-turnaround workloads
assumptions: Baseline request mix: 70% short (<=512 tokens), 25% medium (512-2048), 5% long (>2048)
KV-cache effectiveness: 30% token reuse baseline, adjustable by scenario
Batching: effective per-GPU throughput increases by +40% at average batch 8 for short ops
Utilization target: 55-70% (configurable) to maintain latency headroom
Network egress: accounted separately, 10Gbps per GPU node baseline for planning
On-prem procurement cost estimates: H100-80GB = $60k, A100-40GB = $25k, A10 = $8k (unit purchase price, incl. chassis proforma), node OPEX and power added in monthly column
hardware_options: H100-80GB: best for long-context and very low-latency for large models; high cost; high memory
A100-40GB: balanced price/perf for many generation workloads; good for medium context; widely used
A10 / T4-class: cost-efficient for short-turnaround models and embedding heavy workloads
4-bit quantized variant: can be run on A100/A10 with appropriate kernel changes; reduces VRAM need by ~2-4x depending on model
NVLink-accelerated nodes: recommended when splitting model shards across GPUs for very long contexts
region_profiles: us-west: high demand, prefer lower-latency SKUs; power cost +10% relative baseline
eu-central: balanced demand, higher procurement lead times; buffer +1 rack suggested for surge
ap-southeast: lower baseline qps but high peak volatility, prefer mix of small SKUs to scale horizontally
gov-region: isolated VPC, double-headroom requirement (regulatory), KMS/HSM adds procurement lead time
allocation_matrix_examples: Scenario: Baseline steady-state => 50% A100-40GB, 30% A10, 20% H100 as memory backstop; target util 65% => estimated effective throughput 1.0x baseline
Scenario: 90th-percentile surge => add 25% transient burst nodes (A10) + enable cross-region spill to eu-central; headroom runway = 4 hours at 3x spike
Scenario: Latency-sensitive edge => 70% H100 in-edge racks, 20% A100 central, 10% spare; reserve 15% idle capacity per region for 99th pctl SLAs
Scenario: Cost-optimized quantized => replace 40% A100 with quantized A100 instances, reduce VRAM by avg 2.5x, expect -35% per-token cost but +8-12% 99th tail latency
recommended_bom_by_scenario: Baseline steady-state (1000k daily tokens): 8 H100 nodes, 24 A100 nodes, 12 A10 nodes; 10% spare = +4 nodes; total racks = 6; estimated CAPEX $1.45M; monthly ops (power, SW, support) ~$24k

Surge-ready (3x spikes): baseline + 30 transient A10 nodes in a burst pool; autoscaling policy config listed in linked_artifacts; estimated incremental CAPEX for burst pool reserved (minimal) or equivalent cloud-bursting license cost
Latency-edge config (multi-region): per-region minimum 4 H100 nodes (us-west, eu-central), central pool of 12 A100; CAPEX $1.8M; replication and cross-region failover adds orchestration cost ~$6k/mo

Cost-optimized quantized BOM: swap 40% A100 -> 40% quantized A100 nodes (same chassis), add KV-cache SSD per node 2TB NVMe; CAPEX reduction ~18% vs baseline but include engineering quantization validation cost estimated $75k one-time
headroom_and_runway: Headroom calc method: reserve = max(15% absolute, surge_duration_hours/24 * surge_multiplier_factor), choose greater
Runway metric: hours of 3x baseline sustained with existing spare nodes, tested per-region
Sensitivity: KV-cache hit rate delta +/-10% changes effective capacity by +/-12%; quantization validation risks can reduce effective throughput until tuned
procurement_notes: Lead times: H100 procurement currently ~14-20 weeks depending on vendor and customs; factor into staggered purchasing plan
SKU consolidation: prefer 1-2 SKUs per region to reduce spare parts inventory and COGS; mixed-SKU recommended at global level rather than per-rack
Warranty and spare rotation: plan for 6% spare hardware pool and monthly health cycling scripts to detect pre-failures
estimated_cost_modeling_notes: Per-node monthly OPEX includes power (kWh estimate), network rental, rack space, and Redwood private support add-on. Use configurable multipliers in sheet to reflect local data center pricing.
calc_notes: Throughput and latency modeled using empirical kernels from serving-runtime perf tests (see linked_artifacts). All numbers in this sheet are broad estimates and should be validated with a per-customer perf run using their request mix. Equations: effective_throughput = raw_gpu_tps * (1 + batching_gain) * (1 + kv_cache_hit_rate*kv_gain) * util_target/100
risks_and_open_questions: Quantization risk: accuracy regressions for some LLMs; require eval set and rollback policy
Regional procurement/regulatory delays may force temporary cloud-bursting—contract terms need clarification
Autoscaler behavior: current autoscaler prototype may overshoot during rapid spikes; add cool-down heuristics
